findings.source_quote: ἐὰν ταύτας μὴ φυλάξῃς, ἀλλὰ παρενθυμηθῇς
findings.english_quote: if you do not keep these, but pass them by in your thoughts
findings.issue: The provisional rendering introduces a specific mental action—passing the commandments by in one's thoughts—rather than clearly expressing disregard or neglect of them. This obscures the conduct contrasted with keeping the commandments. The note acknowledges alternatives but does not establish the added mental-action wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “if you do not keep these, but disregard them,” retaining a note that identifies the lexical uncertainty and the alternative “neglect them.” This proposal requires fresh review before adoption.

findings.source_quote: ἔργασαι δικαιοσύνην καὶ ἀρετήν, ἀλήθειαν καὶ φόβον Κυρίου, πίστιν καὶ πρᾳότητα, καὶ ὅσα τούτοις ὅμοιά ἐστιν ἀγαθά.
findings.english_quote: The working full service list is righteousness, virtue, truth, fear of the Lord, faith and gentleness. Lake (1907) Plate VIII retains it. Vulgata printed 65 has a different shorter list; the Latin text printed as Palatina at125 is supplied from Vulgata because the Palatina manuscript is missing this stretch, not independent Palatina support.
findings.issue: The note makes specific assertions about an unseen plate, a Latin reading, and the provenance of supplied Latin without identifying supporting evidence available in this review. It also calls the Latin list “different” and “shorter” without stating its actual contents, so the reader cannot assess the announced alternative. The selected Greek supports the main list, but not these external witness assertions.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected Greek list. Supply a traceable transcription or apparatus citation for the reported Latin alternative, state the actual shorter list, and explicitly attribute the plate and supplementation claims to the project's prior collation rather than presenting them as verified by this review. Where evidence is unavailable, qualify the claims as unverified reports.

findings.source_quote: οὐχ ἕξεις σωτηρίαν, οὔτε τὰ τέκνα σου οὔτε ὁ οἶκός σου
findings.english_quote: Lake (1907) Plate VIII and Vulgata printed 66 retain that warning; the supplied Latin on Palatina printed 127 is Vulgata-derived and is not an independent witness.
findings.issue: The warning is supported by the selected Greek, but the statements about other witnesses and the provenance of their printed text are not established by the supplied source or its selected apparatus. These are external evidentiary claims, not conclusions obtainable from the Greek quotation.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the full warning in the translation. Attribute these witness claims to a documented prior project report and provide its supporting transcription or apparatus reference; otherwise mark them as unverified in the supplied review materials. Preserve the distinction between editorially supplied Latin and independently preserved witness text.

findings.source_quote: ἵνα ἡ μετάνοια αὐτῶν καθαρὰ γένηται τὰς λοιπὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ζωῆς αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Repentance is read in this work’s own moral-change context. Retain pure repentance and the remaining-days condition without imposing a uniform added Godward formula.
findings.issue: This note is labeled “textual_variant,” but it explains a contextual translation decision and gives no alternative source reading. The same misclassification occurs in the note explaining “compel.” This misrepresents interpretive explanations as textual apparatus.
findings.suggested_revision: Classify the repentance and compel notes as lexical or translation-decision notes rather than textual variants. Their substantive explanations can remain, subject to fresh review of the revised records.

findings.english_quote: if you do not keep these, but pass them by in your thoughts
findings.issue: Independently against the Greek, this wording introduces a specific mental action instead of clearly conveying disregard or neglect of the commandments. The simplified reader text therefore retains the same substantive uncertainty rather than making the source's contrast with keeping them intelligible.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “if you do not keep these, but disregard them,” with a concise note identifying “neglect them” as a lexical alternative. Review this proposed replacement directly against the Greek before adoption.

The simplified edition needs its own honest evidentiary qualification; sharing the standard edition's note does not verify it.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve the warning unchanged. Provide or cite the prior evidence behind these witness claims and label them as reported rather than newly verified. Continue distinguishing editorial supplementation from independently preserved text.

findings.issue: The “textual_variant” classification incorrectly identifies this contextual explanation as a source-text variant. The compel note has the same defect. Neither note supplies a competing source reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a lexical or translation-decision classification for both notes, retaining their source-compatible explanations. Review the corrected metadata before acceptance.

summary: Both editions independently cover all six paragraphs and preserve the speakers, necessity, negations, conditional structure, compelled persuasion, and salvation warning extending to children and household. Both follow current servant and contextual repentance policy. Revision is needed for the provisional rendering of παρενθυμηθῇς and for accurate, adequately qualified source notes and metadata. The selected Greek remains the working source; reported variants do not warrant replacing it. This review does not verify unseen plates, manuscripts, Latin editions, or exhaustive collation, and proposed corrections are not automatically accepted.
